articles.title: 'That was his superpower': Faf du Plessis reveals what made MS Dhoni special
articles.summary: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered an insight into what made MS Dhoni stand out as a leader during their time together at Chennai
articles.body: Former South Africa captain Faf du Plessis has offered an insight into what made MS Dhoni stand out as a leader during their time together at Chennai Super Kings (CSK), highlighting the former India captain's instinctive approach to the game and his ability to remain calm under pressure.Du Plessis spent nine seasons with CSK before joining Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2022. Across 154 IPL appearances, he has scored 4,773 runs and won three IPL titles during his time with the Chennai-based franchise. Reflecting on his experience of playing under Dhoni, the Proteas batter explained how the wicketkeeper-batter's ability to read situations and respond instinctively influenced his own approach to captaincy.Speaking on the Prakhar Gupta Podcast, Du Plessis said Dhoni preferred to assess circumstances as they unfolded rather than rely heavily on plans made before a match."This guy has an incredible understanding of the game on the field. He doesn't like to plan too much beforehand and prefers to be instinctive during the match. That was his superpower. He would read the game and the players while staying remarkably calm, as everyone knows he is a very composed person. That's something I want to take from him and apply to my own captaincy," said Faf.MS Dhoni's IPL future hinges on fitnessWhile Du Plessis has reflected on the lessons he learnt from Dhoni, uncertainty continues to surround the former CSK captain's playing future. Dhoni has expressed his desire to feature for the franchise in the next IPL season, but has made it clear that his fitness will determine whether he can continue.Speaking at an event recently, Dhoni said he would assess his physical condition before making a final decision on his participation.“You will know before December,” Dhoni said. “Doc, I will have to go through the test. You will have to give me the report, and then before December, I will have to see, you know, how strong I am to maybe play one more season.”The wicketkeeper-batter, who will turn 46 next year, missed the entire IPL 2026 season because of recurring injuries. His potential return remains a significant talking point for CSK, who have struggled to recapture their earlier success in recent seasons.Dhoni stepped down as captain in 2024, handing over the leadership to Ruturaj Gaikwad. Since then, CSK have failed to reach the playoffs, finishing fifth, tenth and eighth in the points table across the three seasons.Dhoni also responded to the possibility of being unable to continue playing, using humour to underline the importance of getting his fitness right.“And if I am not (fit enough), then, you know, you will have to make sure that you do everything right with me and make sure that this old vintage vehicle is running well on the road. So all the pressure is on them,” Dhoni added, with a hint of light-heartedness, as he often does while responding to questions about his future.CSK's management has previously indicated that the decision rests with Dhoni himself. However, the franchise is also preparing for a major overhaul ahead of the next season, with long-time coach Stephen Fleming departing and Zaheer Khan taking over as his successor.Dhoni's role in the revamped set-up remains uncertain. Whether he returns to the field as a player or takes on a role away from it will depend on his fitness assessment and the decision he makes before December.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli's heartfelt post for 'friend' Harry Kane after Ballon d'Or win
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli on Tuesday congratulated Harry Kane after the England striker won the Ballon d'Or on Monday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Virat Kohli on Tuesday congratulated Harry Kane after the England striker won the Ballon d'Or on Monday. Kohli shared a heartfelt message for his "friend", praising him for his hard work, honesty and determination throughout his football career.Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the prestigious award. The Bayern Munich striker had an outstanding season, scoring 73 goals for club and country and setting new scoring records in Germany.What did Virat Kohli say to Harry Kane?Kohli took to social media to congratulate Kane and wrote a beautiful post."Harry my friend, you deserve every bit of this award for your resilience, hard work and honesty with which you’ve carried yourself through all these years playing football at the top. Really happy for you. God bless you and your family. They must all be very proud of you as you would be of your own journey. My best wishes always. Congratulations @HKane," Kohli wrote.Kane finished ahead of several top players, including Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi, in the voting for the men's award.Kohli set for New Zealand ODIsKohli will next be seen in action in India's five-match ODI series against New Zealand.The star batter heads into the series after an impressive show against the West Indies in September. Kohli scored 168 runs in three matches at an average of 84 and a strike rate of 155.55.He made an unbeaten 139 off just 88 balls in the opening ODI in Thiruvananthapuram, helping India secure a comfortable eight-wicket win. Captain Shubman Gill also played a key role, scoring 110 runs as India chased down the target with ease.During the innings, Kohli crossed 15,000 runs in ODIs, becoming only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to reach the milestone. His 55th ODI century was another reminder of his ability to dominate bowlers.India and New Zealand are scheduled to play five ODIs from November 4 to 15, 2026. The series will begin in Auckland, with the next matches scheduled in Wellington and Hamilton. The final two ODIs will be played in Mount Maunganui.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pathum Nissanka ruled out of Pakistan Test series, Lahiru Udara named replacement
articles.summary: Sri Lanka have suffered a setback ahead of their two-Test series against Pakistan, with opener Pathum Nissanka ruled out after failing to recover from a
articles.body: Sri Lanka have suffered a setback ahead of their two-Test series against Pakistan, with opener Pathum Nissanka ruled out after failing to recover from a left hamstring injury.Nissanka was included in the original 15-member squad on the condition that he would travel only after receiving medical clearance. However, Sri Lanka Cricket confirmed that the opener had not recovered sufficiently to take part in the series.The 27-year-old sustained the injury during Sri Lanka’s white-ball tour of England in September, forcing him to miss the subsequent T20I series against Pakistan. He was later named in the squad for the ongoing ODI tri-series as a conditional selection but was ruled out after failing to prove his fitness.The latest injury setback also delays Nissanka’s return to Test cricket. He had missed Sri Lanka’s home Test series against India in August because of a wrist injury.Lahiru Udara replaces NissankaSri Lanka have named Lahiru Udara as Nissanka’s replacement for the two-Test assignment. Udara is already in Pakistan with the one-day squad, having initially joined the group as Nissanka’s replacement for the tri-series.The opener has featured in five Tests for Sri Lanka and was part of the team’s two most recent assignments in the format against the West Indies and India. He made a significant contribution during the series against the West Indies, scoring 188 in Antigua.The two-Test series against Pakistan forms part of the ongoing ICC World Test Championship cycle and will begin on November 9. The matches are scheduled to be played in Rawalpindi and Lahore, with both teams aiming to improve their positions in the standings.Kusal Mendis to lead Sri LankaKusal Mendis will captain Sri Lanka after being appointed skipper earlier this month. The squad also includes experienced campaigners Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva and Kamindu Mendis.Dilshan Madushanka has earned a recall, while Eshan Malinga and Anjala Bandara have also received call-ups for the series.Sri Lanka currently occupy seventh place in the World Test Championship standings, with Pakistan in ninth. The upcoming fixtures offer both sides an opportunity to gain ground in the competition as the hosts prepare to welcome the visitors for the two Tests.Sri Lanka’s updated squad for Pakistan Tests: Kusal Mendis (captain), Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Sonal Dinusha, Dhananjaya de Silva, Anjala Bandara, Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Milan Rathnayake, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka, Eshan Malinga, Lahiru Udara.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Devdutt Padikkal's 199 in vain as bad light forces draw in India A vs New Zealand A first unofficial Test
articles.summary: India A came agonisingly close to victory but had to settle for a draw against New Zealand A in the first unofficial Test after bad light brought an end
articles.body: India A came agonisingly close to victory but had to settle for a draw against New Zealand A in the first unofficial Test after bad light brought an end to play on Day 4 in Lincoln on Tuesday.New Zealand A were 187/9 in their second innings while chasing a target of 313 when the umpires stopped play due to poor light. India A needed just one more wicket to win, but the conditions did not improve and the match eventually ended in a draw.Curtis Heaphy stood firm for the hosts, remaining unbeaten on 90 off 187 balls, with Jayden Lennox on six. The pair frustrated the Indian bowlers during the final session, helping New Zealand A survive until the close.India A fight back after first-innings collapseIndia A had a difficult start to the match after being bowled out for just 113 in their first innings. Yash Rathod top-scored with an unbeaten 44, while Devdutt Padikkal made 32. Simon Keene led the New Zealand A attack with five wickets, while Zak Gibson picked up three.New Zealand A responded with 317, taking a first-innings lead of 204 runs. Captain Rhys Mariu scored 76, while Dean Foxcroft contributed 51. Kristian Clarke added 42, helping the hosts build a strong advantage.Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj took three wickets each for India A, while Akash Deep claimed two.Padikkal leads India's fightbackIndia A produced a strong response in their second innings, scoring 516 to set New Zealand A a target of 313. Padikkal was the standout performer with the bat, scoring 199 off 248 balls, including 24 fours and three sixes. He shared a 215-run partnership with Sai Sudharsan, who scored 91, to put India A back in the contest. Yash Rathod also made an important contribution with 66, while Washington Sundar scored 52. Auqib Nabi chipped in with 38, and Akash Deep remained unbeaten on 25.Padikkal missed out on a double-century by just one run after being given out caught behind. His innings, however, helped India A turn the match around after their disappointing first-innings performance.India A fall just shortChasing 313 for victory, New Zealand A lost three early wickets, with Auqib Nabi striking twice in the opening overs before dismissing Matthew Boyle. The hosts were soon under pressure, but Foxcroft's 42 offered some resistance.Mukesh Choudhary dismissed Foxcroft, while Anshul Kamboj removed wicketkeeper Mitchell Hay. Washington Sundar then sent back Kristian Clarke before Padikkal made an impact with the ball, taking his maiden first-class wicket by dismissing Fraser Sheat. He later removed Zak Gibson to leave New Zealand A at 160/8.Akash Deep bowled Simon Keene for five, leaving India A just one wicket away from victory.However, Heaphy and Lennox held on as bad light stopped play at 187/9 after 65 overs.Auqib Nabi finished with three wickets in the second innings, while Padikkal claimed two. Akash Deep, Mukesh Choudhary, Anshul Kamboj and Sundar took one wicket each.The two teams will now turn their attention to the second unofficial Test, scheduled to begin on Saturday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs South Africa: Steve Smith ruled out of Cape Town Test due to neck injury
articles.summary: Steve Smith was a late injury omission for Australia ahead of the series-deciding third Test against South Africa on Tuesday; the 37-year-old had been set to play at Cape Town for the first time since the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal; watch the third Test live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Australia gave the 37-year-old a chance to prove his fitness ahead of the Test match, which would have seen Smith return to Cape Town for the first time since the infamous 'Sandpapergate' scandal at Newlands in 2018.

Smith appeared to injure himself during his first spell at the crease during Australia's second Test defeat to South Africa in Gqeberha, in which the hosts levelled the series 1-1.

The former skipper subsequently dropped down the batting order in the second innings, as Pat Cummins' side went on to suffer an innings and 31-run defeat.

Ahead of the third Test, Smith had complained of neck stiffness during Australia's pre-match training session and was due to undergo a fitness test ahead of Tuesday's match.

He was later seen walking around Newlands with a large plaster stuck to his neck.

Cummins said that their star batter had been working to overcome the injury early on Tuesday morning, but confirmed at the toss that Smith would be one of four changes to the Australia XI.

"He had a little try this morning," Cummins told SuperSport. "But he wasn't happy with how his neck was feeling, so we had to look elsewhere."

Smith, who received 12-month suspension for his role as Australia's captain in the ball-tampering scandal, has had a lean tour of South Africa.

His top score of 28 came during Australia's first innings in Gqeberha, with Smith having made 25 and 27 during the opening Test in Durban.

Cameron Green returns to the side and slots in at No 4 in place of Smith. Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Nathan Lyon also come into the starting XI.

Beau Webster, Scott Boland and Nic Maddinson miss out, while Matt Renshaw opens for Australia in Maddinson's place.

Australia won the toss and elected to field first, with Cummins stating he was hopeful his batters can bounce back after South Africa's bowlers kept them to a first-innings score of 99 in the second Test.

"We've got some guys really well placed," Cummins said. "They've been here working hard the last couple of weeks.

"A couple of injuries they're coming back from and are now 100 per cent. It's exciting, it's a huge opportunity and everyone's itching to get out there."

articles.title: India seal T20I series victory vs New Zealand with two games to spare as Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi star
articles.summary: India sealed a T20I series victory against New Zealand with two games to spare on Tuesday; Abhishek Sharma struck a 35-ball hundred to guide the visitors to a six-wicket victory in the third T20I in Wellington
articles.body:
Sharma, who scored the fastest T20I century against a Test-playing nation with a 30-ball ton against Afghanistan last month, was on track to surpass that feat but narrowly fell short as he brought up 113 runs off 38 deliveries.

India were set a target of 199 runs to win the third T20I and chased it down in 13.2 overs, with Sharma and 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi combining to hit the fastest team 50 in the white-ball format in just 2.2 overs.

"I think the key was pretty simple," Sharma said. "Me and Vaibhav were just going to enjoy ourselves for a bit in the power play.

"When we were fielding, we were observing the pitch. There was a bit of extra bounce, and with the dimensions of the ground we could use the power play and the pace of the ball. The plan was just to get momentum for the team."

Daryl Mitchell top-scored for the hosts in the first innings with an unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, while Finn Allen (40) and Bevon Jacobs (39no) followed up to push the hosts just shy of the 200-run mark.

Sharma and Sooryavanshi later arrived and put on a stand of 133 off 44 deliveries, before the latter was caught out by Mitchell at long on off a Matthew Fisher delivery.

Fisher almost had a second wicket three balls later after Mitchell Santner dropped Sharma on 92 at extra cover.

New Zealand would eventually remove the India batter in the 10th over, with Sharma hitting Kyle Jamieson up to Glenn Phillips, waiting at deep mid-wicket.

Santner later removed Iyer for five after he sent a delivery to Glenn Phillips at deep mid-wicket, before Jamieson had his second, bowling Sanju Samson for 18.

The result sees India seal back-to-back T20I series victories against New Zealand, following their 4-1 win on home soil in January.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India delivered a breathtaking batting performance in the third T20I against New Zealand at Wellington’s Hnry Stadium on Tuesday, rewriting
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India delivered a breathtaking batting performance in the third T20I against New Zealand at Wellington’s Hnry Stadium on Tuesday, rewriting several records with an extraordinary display of aggression.The standout moment came during the chase of 199, when Abhishek Sharma and promoted batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi tore into the New Zealand bowling attack.The duo powered India to an unprecedented 118 without loss in the first six overs, setting a new world record for the highest powerplay total in men’s T20 internationals.India surpassed Romania’s previous record of 116 without losing a wicket against Serbia in Sofia in 2021, underlining the remarkable scale of their batting assault.With the hosts struggling to contain the onslaught, both Indian batters scored at an astonishing rate. Abhishek remained unbeaten on 57 off just 20 deliveries, while Sooryavanshi contributed an unbeaten 44 from 17 balls, putting India firmly in control of the contest.Highest powerplay totals in men's T20IsThe following are the highest team totals recorded during the first six overs in men's T20Is, where data is available:118/0 – India vs New Zealand, Wellington, 2026116/0 – Romania vs Serbia, Sofia, 2021 (5.4 overs)113/1 – Australia vs Scotland, Edinburgh, 2024103/1 – Zimbabwe vs Gambia, Nairobi (RSC), 2024102/0 – South Africa vs West Indies, Centurion, 2023100/0 – England vs South Africa, Old Trafford, 2025100/0 – India vs Afghanistan, Delhi, 2026India's extraordinary start was not limited to the powerplay record. The visitors also crossed the 100-run mark in just five overs, making it the second-fastest team hundred in men's T20I cricket, according to the reported figures.Only Eswatini have reached the milestone faster, having scored 100 runs in 4.5 overs against Mozambique earlier in 2026. Among Full Member nations, India's achievement stands out as the fastest, surpassing the previous marks set by South Africa and Australia, both of whom reached three figures in 5.3 overs against their respective opponents.The Indian team also raced to its half-century in only 2.2 overs, matching the joint-fastest team fifty recorded in men's T20Is. Papua New Guinea achieved the same feat against Vanuatu, while Romania also reached 50 in 2.2 overs against Serbia.India seal dominant series leadNew Zealand posted 198/3 in their allotted 20 overs, setting India a target of 199. However, the Indian batters made the chase look remarkably straightforward, reaching 199/4 in just 13.2 overs.India ultimately secured a six-wicket victory with 40 balls to spare, taking an unassailable 3-0 lead in the series in Wellington. Despite needing a little luck to finish the contest, the visitors' dominant performance with the bat ensured another emphatic result.The record-breaking powerplay was the defining feature of the match, highlighting India's aggressive approach and their ability to put opposition bowling attacks under immense pressure from the very beginning.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ: Ton-up Abhishek Sharma surpasses Virat Kohli in major T20 record
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display, smashing a 35-ball century to power India to a six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display, smashing a 35-ball century to power India to a six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third T20I on Tuesday. The left-handed opener blazed his way to 113 off just 38 deliveries as India chased down the target with 40 balls to spare, taking an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.Abhishek's sensational knock featured nine fours and 11 sixes, helping him surpass Virat Kohli to become India's leading century-maker in men's T20 cricket. The 24-year-old now has 11 hundreds in the format, moving ahead of Kohli, who has 10.The Indian opener also joined the elite list of the most prolific century-makers in men's T20 cricket, moving into third place behind Chris Gayle and Babar Azam.Abhishek Sharma surpasses Kohli in T20 hundredsAbhishek continued his remarkable run in the shortest format with a blistering innings that left the New Zealand bowlers searching for answers. He reached his century in just 35 balls, dismantling the attack with an extraordinary combination of power and timing.His 113-run knock came off 38 deliveries and included 11 sixes, underlining his dominance at the crease. The Indian opener was eventually dismissed by Kyle Jamieson, with Glenn Phillips completing the catch at deep mid-wicket, but the damage had already been done.With his 11th T20 hundred, Abhishek moved past Kohli's tally of 10 centuries for India. Globally, only Chris Gayle, with 22 hundreds, and Babar Azam, with 13, have scored more centuries in men's T20 cricket.Most hundreds in men's T20 cricket22 — Chris Gayle13 — Babar Azam11 — Abhishek Sharma10 — Quinton de Kock10 — Virat Kohli10 — David WarnerAbhishek and Sooryavanshi rewrite the Powerplay recordIndia made a change at the top of the order, sending young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to open alongside Abhishek. The move paid spectacular dividends as the duo launched an all-out assault on the New Zealand bowling attack.India raced to 118 runs in the Powerplay, setting a new record for the highest Powerplay total by a Full Member nation in men's T20 internationals. The opening partnership eventually yielded 133 runs, putting India firmly in control of the chase.While Sooryavanshi missed out on a half-century, he provided explosive support to Abhishek, who continued to attack relentlessly. The youngster was eventually dismissed by Matthew Fisher, who claimed his maiden T20I wicket.New Zealand's decision to hold back captain Mitchell Santner from bowling against the two left-handed openers proved costly. By the time the spinner came into the attack, India had already seized complete control of the contest.The hosts conceded 118 runs in the first six overs and 178 in the first 10, leaving their bowlers with little room to recover. Jamieson and Santner picked up wickets towards the end, but the contest was effectively decided during the opening assault.Mitchell's unbeaten 89 helps New Zealand post competitive totalEarlier, India captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and elected to bowl first, hoping to put New Zealand under pressure. The hosts lost Tim Seifert early, but Finn Allen and Daryl Mitchell responded with an aggressive counter-attack to give their side a strong platform.Allen fell in the 40s, but Mitchell continued to anchor the innings and finished unbeaten on 89. Bevon Jacobs also contributed a useful knock, helping New Zealand build a competitive total.India's bowling performance was mixed, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar once again struggling to make a significant impact. However, the visitors recovered well at the death, with Prince Yadav producing an impressive comeback and Arshdeep Singh and Nitish Kumar Reddy executing their yorkers effectively.Their disciplined death bowling ensured New Zealand could not push their total beyond the 200-run mark, leaving India with a target of 199 runs.The victory handed India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, with two matches still to be played. After dominating the contest with the bat, the visitors completed the chase with 40 deliveries remaining.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma's 35-ball century powers India to series-clinching win over New Zealand
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing a 35-ball century as India defeated New Zealand by six wickets in the third
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking display of power-hitting, smashing a 35-ball century as India defeated New Zealand by six wickets in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.The left-handed opener hammered 113 off just 38 deliveries, striking 11 sixes and nine fours as India chased down New Zealand's target of 199 in only 13.2 overs, with 40 balls to spare.Sharma received explosive support from 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi as the pair tore into the New Zealand attack from the outset. Jacob Duffy conceded 26 runs in the opening over, followed by 17 and 21 in the next two as India raced to 64 without loss in three overs.The onslaught intensified as India plundered 20 runs in the fourth over, 16 in the fifth and another 18 in the sixth to finish the Powerplay at a staggering 118 without losing a wicket. Sharma reached his fifty off just 15 balls.Matthew Fisher eventually broke the opening stand in the eighth over, dismissing Sooryavanshi for a blistering 45 off 19 deliveries, including four sixes and four fours. However, Sharma continued his assault alongside Sanju Samson, taking India to 156/1 after eight overs.After a relatively quiet ninth over, Sharma brought up his century off 35 balls against Kyle Jamieson in the 10th over. He eventually fell to Jamieson for 113 off 38 deliveries, but India were already firmly in control.The chase briefly lost momentum as Shreyas Iyer and Samson departed towards the end. India, however, comfortably crossed the finish line in 13.2 overs to register a commanding victory.Jamieson claimed two wickets, while Fisher and Mitchell Santner took one apiece. None of New Zealand's bowlers managed to keep their economy rate below 12 runs per over.Mitchell, Jacobs lift New Zealand to 198/3Earlier, Daryl Mitchell's unbeaten 89 off 52 balls helped New Zealand post 198/3 after India opted to bowl. Bevon Jacobs provided a brisk finish with 39 off 23 deliveries as the pair added an unbeaten 75-run stand for the fourth wicket.New Zealand lost Tim Seifert early, with Arshdeep Singh dismissing the opener for two. Finn Allen and Mitchell then rebuilt the innings, putting together 86 runs before Nitish Kumar Reddy removed Allen for 40 off 25 balls, an innings featuring five sixes.Glenn Phillips, playing his 100th T20I, could manage only 17 before Axar Patel dismissed him in the 12th over. Mitchell and Jacobs subsequently ensured the hosts finished with a competitive total, although India's bowlers restricted the scoring in the latter half of the innings.Arshdeep, Axar and Nitish picked up a wicket each, while Bhuvneshwar Kumar went wicketless.India rewrite the record booksIndia's emphatic chase ranked among the quickest successful pursuits of a target of at least 190 in T20 cricket. Their 199-run chase, completed with 40 balls remaining, was second on the all-team list behind Estonia's successful pursuit of 192 against Cyprus in 2024, which left 42 balls unused.Among full-member nations, it surpassed India's previous record against New Zealand in Raipur earlier this year, when they chased 209 with 28 balls to spare.Sharma's century, completed in 35 balls, also placed him among the fastest centurions in T20Is involving full-member teams. He had previously struck a 30-ball hundred against Afghanistan in Delhi earlier in 2026.The opening partnership between Sharma and Sooryavanshi was equally remarkable, scoring at a run rate of 18.13, the highest for a century stand by openers involving full-member teams in men's T20Is.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Abhishek Sharma hits 35-ball century as India seal T20 series win over New Zealand
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma's 113 from 38 balls helps India chase a target of 199 in just 13.2 overs against New Zealand.
articles.body:
New Zealand 198-3 (20 overs): Mitchell 89 (52); Singh 1-33

India 199-4 (13.2 overs): Abhishek 113 (38); Jamieson 2-45

India won by six wickets; lead series 3-0

Abhishek Sharma struck a 35-ball century in India's astonishing chase of 199 in just 13.2 overs in the third T20 against New Zealand in Wellington.

Abhishek and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blitzed 133 in seven overs for the first wicket, with their powerplay score of 118 setting a new record for international T20s.

Fifteen-year-old Sooryavanshi's 45 from 19 balls was merely a supporting act to Abhishek, who raced to his fifty from 15 deliveries as New Zealand's bowlers wilted.

After the youngster's departure in the eighth over, Abhishek helped India cruise towards their target, falling for 113 from 38 balls - which included nine fours and 11 sixes.

He fell short of equalling his record for India's fastest T20 hundred, which came off 30 balls against Afghanistan last month.

India's middle order then ticked off the remaining 21 runs required with ease, with New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner's figures of 1-17 off three overs an outlier in a painful match for bowlers.

The Black Caps' 198-3 was set up by Daryl Mitchell's 89 from 52 balls and Finn Allen added 40 off 25, and their total looked competitive until India barely broke a sweat in their pursuit.

The result gives India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, which is followed by five one-day internationals and two Tests.

articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma credited meticulous preparation and a clear game plan for his sensational century against New Zealand, revealing that he had “manifested”
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma credited meticulous preparation and a clear game plan for his sensational century against New Zealand, revealing that he had “manifested” the innings before producing a breathtaking performance in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday.The left-handed opener smashed 113 off just 38 balls, helping India chase down 199 in only 13.2 overs. The six-wicket victory gave India an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.Abhishek and teenage opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who scored 45 off 19 deliveries, combined to register a record-breaking 118 without loss in the powerplay, the highest total recorded in the first six overs of a men's T20 international.Speaking after receiving the Player of the Match award, Abhishek explained how the opening pair approached the chase.“I think the key was pretty simple. It was just me and Vaibhav, just going to enjoy there for a bit, especially in the powerplay,” he told broadcasters.The Indian opener said the duo assessed the pitch while fielding and identified opportunities to exploit Wellington's short square boundaries and the pace of New Zealand's bowlers.“Especially when we were fielding, we were observing the pitch a bit because of this extra bounce. But I feel the dimensions of the ground, we could use the powerplay, and we could use their pace as well. So that was the easy plan,” he added.Preparation behind the explosive inningsAbhishek stressed that such performances are rarely accidental, highlighting the work he puts in during training and the support he receives from India's coaching staff.“I feel it's not that, I wouldn't say it's that easy, but it's just the preparation behind the scenes. Special mention to our coaches because of the sidearms; we've been playing them a lot,” he said.The batter explained that understanding the conditions and adapting to the opposition's bowling plans were central to his approach.“Preparation is really important as a batter. If you see the conditions and the dimensions, that's always in your mind, and then you have to keep the bowlers also in your mind and play the shots according to the bowlers,” Abhishek said.After revealing that India had enjoyed a productive training session the previous day, he described how the performance matched his expectations.“We had a good practice session yesterday, and I just wanted to utilise it, and that's what I did. And I feel I pretty much manifested this innings, and it happened,” he added.Abhishek reached his half-century in just 15 balls before completing his hundred in 35 deliveries, making the innings one of the standout performances of his T20 career.Yuvraj Singh's playful challengeThe knock also prompted a cheeky message from Abhishek's mentor, former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh.On social media platform X, Yuvraj challenged his protégé to surpass his record for India's fastest T20I half-century, which came off just 12 balls against England during the 2007 T20 World Cup.“You still can’t get 50 off 12, can you, Abhishek Sharma! Looks like two left-handers batting in their backyard!” Yuvraj wrote.Responding to the challenge, Abhishek acknowledged the difficulty of achieving such a feat and praised his mentor's remarkable hitting ability.“I don't know what cricket he was playing back at that time, but it's not that easy at all,” he said, explaining that scoring 50 in 12 balls requires exceptional circumstances.“It just happens once in a while. But, obviously, as a batter, we don't go for that milestone. We always want to win the game for the team, me and especially Vaibhav. He's here. So that was the plan, and that's what we want to take throughout the series as well, and it went well,” he added.Yuvraj later returned to social media to praise Abhishek's remarkable scoring rate, Sooryavanshi's contribution and India's overall performance.“And I can’t make 100 off 30 or 34 balls. Well played sir Abhishek Sharma! Great innings aur apne single bhi le liye,” he wrote, congratulating the team on its series victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England eliminated from ODI tri-series as Sri Lanka's bowlers dominate in victory against Pakistan to book final spot
articles.summary: Sri Lanka claim eight-wicket victory against Pakistan on Tuesday to book their spot in the final of the ODI tri-series; the win ends England's hopes of qualifying; watch England's final match vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am, Thursday (first ball 8am)
articles.body:
After suffering three defeats at the tournament, Brendon McCullum's side were left on the brink of elimination and needed Pakistan to win on Tuesday and a victory against Sri Lanka in their final round-robin match on Thursday to stand a chance of advancing.

Instead, Sri Lanka will now face Pakistan in the final on Saturday, October 31, after Gary Kirsten's side, who won the toss and elected to bowl, dismissed the hosts for 110 in 25.3 overs - Pakistan's second-lowest ODI total at home.

After captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to field, Dilshan Madushanka starred, taking career-best ODI figures of five for 34.

Kamindu Mendis later led his side to victory, hitting an unbeaten 62 off 60 deliveries, as Sri Lanka chased down Pakistan's total inside 18.1 overs.

Pakistan's top-order struggles were highlighted again on Tuesday, with four of their five specialist batters making single figures.

"Unfortunately, for the last three or four games we are collapsing at the top order," captain Shaheen Shah Afridi said.

"We have three days now and we can practice. We will come back in the final and bat stronger. We need to forget this game quickly and take the positives from the previous games."

Fakhar Zaman was dismissed for five runs off 13 deliveries by Madushanka inside four overs, before Maaz Sadaqat was pinned lbw for eight by Asitha Fernando.

Madushanka had his second not long after, forcing Saad Baig (5) to clip a ball to short cover, where he was caught by Janith Liyanage.

Salman Agha (9), Babar Azam (29), and Shadab Khan (2) all followed in the space of three overs, leaving Pakistan 64-6.

Another flurry of wickets followed, with Dunith Wellalage forcing Arafat Minhas to edge behind to Mendis, before Madushanka removed all of Hasan Nawaz (17), Harris Rauf (1) and Afridi (15).

Kamindu arrived at the crease and attacked ruthlessly, making eight fours and two sixes.

His opening partner, Avishka Fernando, fell for 16 off 17, before Kusal later departed for eight. Pavan Rathnayake saw out the innings alongside Mendis, making an unbeaten 23.

articles.title: England in Pakistan: Harry Brook's side out after Sri Lanka beat hosts
articles.summary: Sri Lanka thrash Pakistan by eight wickets to end England's hopes of reaching Saturday's tri-series final.
articles.body:
One-day international tri-series, Lahore

Pakistan 110 (25.2 overs): Babar 29; Madushanka 5-34

Sri Lanka 114-2 (18.1 overs): Kaminudu 62*

England are out of their 50-over tri-series in Pakistan after the hosts were beaten by Sri Lanka on Tuesday in Lahore.

After three defeats from three, Harry Brook's side needed Pakistan to beat Sri Lanka to have a chance of reaching Saturday's final by beating Sri Lanka on Thursday.

Instead, that match will be a dead rubber after Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out and Sri Lanka raced to their target in just 18.1 overs.

Though conditions will be significantly different at next year's World Cup in southern Africa, the exit is a blow to England, who had built some momentum in their one-day international cricket this year.

After their dismal World Cup defence in 2023 and exiting the Champions Trophy without winning a match last year, England had won away in Sri Lanka and beaten India and Sri Lanka at home in 2026.

In Pakistan, they failed to chase 303 despite being well placed at 120-1 and then suffered two extraordinary losses.

After their tournament concludes on Thursday, England travel to Australia for a tour of three ODIs and five T20s, starting on 13 November.

They are also scheduled to play a warm-up against a Western Australia XI on Saturday, 7 November in Perth.

For Sri Lanka, left-armer Dilshan Madushanka landed blows before Saturday's final by taking 5-34 against Pakistan.

articles.body: Sri Lanka delivered a commanding eight-wicket victory over Pakistan on Tuesday, producing a clinical all-round performance to knock England out of contention for the ODI tri-series final. Fast bowler Dilshan Madushanka led the charge with a career-best five-wicket haul before Kamindu Mendis anchored a comfortable chase, giving Sri Lanka a timely boost ahead of the title clash.Madushanka's career-best five-for dismantles PakistanMadushanka returned figures of 5-34 as Pakistan were bowled out for just 110 after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to field at the Gaddafi Stadium. Pakistan, who had already secured their place in the final, struggled to cope with Madushanka's bowling as Sri Lanka's attack dismantled their batting line-up. The hosts were unable to build a substantial partnership, leaving Sri Lanka with a modest target to chase.Kamindu Mendis anchors comfortable chaseIn reply, Sri Lanka raced to 114-2 in just 18.1 overs, completing the chase well before the floodlight towers were fully switched on for the day-night encounter.Kamindu starred with an unbeaten 62 off 60 deliveries, striking eight fours and two sixes. He survived an early reprieve after being dropped by the wicketkeeper before opening his account and later overturned an on-field lbw decision on 44 after successfully reviewing the call.The left-hander brought up his half-century in memorable fashion, pulling a delivery for six after substitute fielder Ghazi Ghori had touched the boundary with his foot while completing a catch.Sri Lanka bounce back as England crash outSri Lanka's emphatic win came after their remarkable chase of 430 against England in Rawalpindi, the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history. articles.title: 'Bowler can control the game': Bhuvneshwar Kumar on T20 cricket's batting boom and six-hitting revolution
articles.summary: With T20 cricket increasingly defined by aggressive batting, shorter boundaries and relentless scoring, the margin for error for bowlers has become
articles.body: With T20 cricket increasingly defined by aggressive batting, shorter boundaries and relentless scoring, the margin for error for bowlers has become slimmer than ever. However, veteran India pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar believes that quality bowling and adaptability can still make a decisive difference, insisting that the format is not entirely tilted in favour of batters.The 36-year-old, who has returned to India's international setup after nearly four years, shared his views following India's victory in the third T20I. Bhuvneshwar earned his comeback on the back of impressive performances in the IPL, where he has adapted his skills to meet the evolving demands of the shortest format.'A bowler can control the game'"I know that the margin of error is very low, which we generally talk about. But still, a bowler can land the ball wherever he wants to. I strongly believe that a bowler can control the game," Bhuvneshwar told reporters.Bhuvneshwar acknowledged that modern T20 cricket offers several advantages to batters, including smaller boundaries and an increasingly aggressive approach. However, he maintained that bowlers who execute their plans and adapt quickly can still dictate the course of a match."This is a debatable question. We say that the conditions favour the batters nowadays and all that, but I still believe that a bowler can control the game. The reason is that we feed the ball to the batter," he said."There are small boundaries. Everything is given to the batters. But still, a bowler is the one who feeds the ball to the batter. Then it's up to the batter what he wants to play, whether he wants to play according to the ball or not.""But still, if you look at the good bowlers, they are still doing well. They are consistent. Even if the game is not equal, the bowler adapts quickly. We've seen it in IPL, we've seen it here as well," he added.Bhuvneshwar not looking too far ahead after India comebackDespite returning to the international setup after a prolonged absence, Bhuvneshwar is not looking too far ahead in his career. The experienced pacer said he intends to continue playing domestic cricket and focus on performing consistently rather than setting long-term international targets."It is great to be playing for India again but I am not thinking too much about the future. I will continue to play domestic cricket, whether it is Mushtaq Ali or Vijay Hazare," he said.Bhuvneshwar also credited his performances in the IPL over the past two years for opening the door to his return, adding that he had not actively chased an India comeback even though representing the country had always remained his dream."I did not chase this (playing for India again) though it was always the dream. Credit goes to my performances in the IPL over the past two years," he added.'Batters are looking to hit every ball'Bhuvneshwar also highlighted the changing mindset of batters, noting that modern players are increasingly unwilling to ease off even after scoring quickly at the start of an over. He recalled how batters previously tended to consolidate after striking a few boundaries, whereas the current generation continues to attack throughout the innings."Earlier, somewhere there was a thinking that as runs have come in the first couple of balls, let's go easy in the remaining over. But now it is not like that. Batters are looking to hit every ball," he said."There is one ball. There are two balls. There are six balls. Credit should be given to this generation for playing fearlessly," Bhuvneshwar added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BCCI asks state units to support differently-abled cricketers
articles.summary: Mumbai: In a significant step towards making cricket more inclusive, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has urged all 38 state cricket associations to take
articles.body: Mumbai: In a significant step towards making cricket more inclusive, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has urged all 38 state cricket associations to take measures to support differently-abled cricketers and promote the development of the game in their respective jurisdictions.In a communication sent to all member associations on Monday, a copy of which is with The Times of India, Saikia referred to the decision taken at the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM), held in Mumbai on September 18, 2026, and called on the state units to take steps towards the welfare and development of differently-abled players."As deliberated and agreed during the 95th Annual General Meeting of the BCCI, held in Mumbai on September 18, 2026, all the member associations are requested to take appropriate measures towards the welfare, development and the betterment of differently-abled cricketers within their respective jurisdictions," Saikia wrote.He further urged the associations to create opportunities for differently-abled players to participate in the sport and improve their skills."Member associations are requested to take meaningful initiatives to promote the participation of differently-abled cricketers and to provide them with due encouragement, assistance and opportunities to grow in the game," the BCCI secretary stated.Concluding his letter, Saikia highlighted the importance of cooperation among the state units in advancing the cause of inclusive cricket."Your cooperation and support in this endeavor will go a long way in strengthening the spirit of inclusivity and furthering the development of cricket for differently-abled cricketers across the country," he wrote.At the conclusion of its AGM, the BCCI had also highlighted the decision in its communication to the media, stating: "The General Body discussed with the State Units, measures to support differently-abled cricketers, including appropriate facilities and resources to promote their development and progress."Ravi Chauhan, general secretary of the Differently Abled Cricket Council of India (DCCI), welcomed the move, describing it as an important milestone for the sport."I welcome this decision by the BCCI. Differently-abled cricket is being played in India for the last 40 years. For the last five years or so, the BCCI has supported the DCCI, thanks to Jay bhai (ICC chairman & ex-BCCI secretary Jay Shah). The BCCI's move (to support differently-abled cricketers) in the BCCI's 95th AGM was a milestone decision. I thank the secretary of BCCI for writing to all the state associations to support and run differently-abled cricket in their states," Chauhan told TOI on Tuesday.He said the decision would encourage players across the country and expressed hope that the BCCI would extend the same kind of support to differently-abled cricket that it has provided to women's cricket in recent years."The differently-abled cricketers of India are very happy with the BCCI's decision, and will get hugely encouraged from it. I hope that the BCCI promotes different-abled cricket the way it has promoted women's cricket in the last few years. I hope that one day, the differently-abled cricketers will have a league of their own, and they will get an official recognition. I hope that the state associations start working towards the betterment of different-abled cricket, so that it becomes part of the mainstream sport," he added.Abhay Pratap Singh also welcomed the BCCI's initiative, expressing gratitude to the board and its leadership for recognising the importance of inclusive cricket and encouraging the development of differently-abled players."We express our sincere gratitude to the BCCI and its leadership for this encouraging initiative towards the welfare and development of differently-abled cricketers. This is a significant step towards making cricket more inclusive and ensuring that talented players get the encouragement, support and opportunities they deserve. The BCCI’s communication to its member associations reflects a positive commitment to strengthening differently-abled cricket in India. We hope this initiative will inspire associations across the country to take concrete measures to support these cricketers and help them reach their full potential," Singh said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Namibia v Ireland: Tourists fall behind in ODI series after defeat in Windhoek
articles.summary: Ireland fall 2-1 behind in their five-match ODI series against Namibia as they lose by 63 runs in the third meeting between the sides.
articles.body:
Namibia 316-7 (50 overs): Frylinck 126, Erasmus 54, Kruger 42, Volschenck 36; McBrine 2-53, Campher 2-68

Ireland 253 all out (44.5 overs): Campher 106; Scholtz 2-31, Trumpelmann 2-37, Brassell 2-72

Ireland fell 2-1 behind in their five-match one-day international series against Namibia as they lost the third meeting between the sides by 63 runs in Windhoek on Tuesday.

Curtis Campher's century proved insufficient for the tourists, who were all out for 253 in the 45th over as they attempted to chase down their opponent's total of 316-7.

Ireland skipper Paul Stirling was unable to bat after injuring his finger in the field during the home side's innings.

Jan Frylinck shone for Namibia as he top-scored with 126 to lay the platform for the victory.

The sides will meet again on Friday and Sunday as Ireland continue their preparations for next year's World Cup qualifiers.

After winning the toss and opting to bat first, opener Louren Steenkamp's departure for 13 left Namibia 33-1.

When Malan Kruger (42) lost his wicket, the hosts sat 81-2 but a third-wicket partnership of 101 between Frylinck and captain Gerhard Erasmus (54) got their side back on track to achieve their impressive total.

Alex Volschenk chipped in with 36, while Campher and Andy McBrine were the pick of the Ireland bowlers with two wickets apiece.

In response, Ireland struggled at 56-4 before Campher's 106 off 86 balls put them in with a chance of securing what at one stage looked like an improbable victory.

Ultimately, their reply fell short however as wickets continued to fall regularly and they were all out with 31 balls of their innings still remaining.

Bernard Scholtz, Ruben Trumpelmann and Jack Brassell each took two wickets.

articles.summary: MYSURU: Exploiting an opponent’s weakness is par for the course in sport.
articles.body: MYSURU: Exploiting an opponent’s weakness is par for the course in sport. Karnataka were expected to do just that against Tripura, but have missed a trick or two. After letting the visitors off the hook on the opening day of their Ranji Trophy Group B match at the SDNRW Ground here, the hosts failed to make the most of promising starts on Tuesday, leaving themselves with plenty of work to do despite securing their first innings lead of the season. At stumps, Karnataka were 297/7, ahead by 103 runs.In normal circumstances, three points from a drawn game could have been acceptable. But, as head coach R Vinay Kumar pointed out, this is a must-win match. With just two points from as many games, Karnataka need a victory to keep their knockout hopes alive.In a game of fine margins, Karnataka have been struggling to get ahead. Tuesday was another case in point. Against a bowling attack that was, at best, ordinary, the hosts had an opportunity to build a substantial lead, with both young batters keen to make a mark and seasoned campaigners at the crease. Instead, they scored at just 3.2 runs an over and lost wickets at regular intervals on a surface where the odd ball kept low.Resuming at 10/1, rookie Rohan Patil (72; 130b, 9x4) and Vyshak Vijaykumar adopted a cautious approach and nearly saw off the first hour. However, Vyshak fell while attempting to drive a fuller delivery from Sandeep Sarkar, edging it to wicketkeeper Sentu Sarkar. Karnataka had managed just 36 runs by the 20th over.Rohan and KV Aneesh (68; 142b, 6x4) then added 82 for the third wicket, showing patience against the Tripura attack, which didn’t command that kind of an approach.Rohan, known more as a big-hitting white-ball specialist, brought up his maiden first-class half-century off 88 balls with a back-foot punch through the covers. His promising knock ended when he attempted to flick a fuller delivery from Abhijith Sarkar (3/59) and was trapped leg-before.The arrival of seasoned campaigner Karun Nair (68; 85b, 8x4) injected urgency into the innings, his fluent strokeplay unsettling the bowlers. Dropped on 11 by wicketkeeper Sentu off Bikram Debnath, Karun made the most of the reprieve before Sandip Sarkar (2/83) trapped him leg-before as he played forward. His partnership with Aneesh yielded 105 runs, blending aggression with caution.Aneesh, who had looked well set, soon followed, miscuing a short ball from Parvez Sultan to Sandip at midwicket. Skipper Shreyas Gopal (19) was bowled by Sultan, while KL Shrijith (13), who had begun to find his rhythm with a classic sweep for six off Sandip, offered a regulation catch to Bikram Das at cover off Abhijith.Aneeshwar Gautam (33 batting) and Manvanth Kumar (6 batting) saw off the remaining overs, with the latter striking two sixes over long-on and midwicket.While the advantage still firmly rests with Karnataka, the next two days will be about how they can turn into a much-needed victory.SCOREBOARDTripura (I innings): 194.Karnataka (I innings; o/n 10/1): Rohan Patil lbw a Sarkar 72, Vyshak Vijaykumar c C Sarkar b S Sarkar 12, KV Anesh c S Sarkar b Sultan 68, Karun Nair lbw S Sarkar 63, Aneeshwar Gautam (batting) 33, Shreyas Gopal b Sultan 19, KL Shrijith c B Das b A Sarkar 13, Manvanth Kumar (batting) 6. articles.body: KOCHI: Australian captain Sophie Molineux, hard-hitting Indian wicketkeeper batter G Kamalini, and all-rounder Sneh Rana, will headline 146 players in the Women’s Premier League (WPL) auction pool as the hammer falls in Kochi on Wednesday. Of the shortlisted players, 119 are Indian and 27 are from overseas. The five franchises will be looking to fill 27 slots at the mini-auction with a total purse of Rs 8.15 cr. The fifth edition of the WPL is scheduled to begin from Jan 14, 2027.Kamalini on Mumbai's radarSlots: SixPurse: Rs 0.90 crMumbai arrive with a settled nucleus of Amelia Kerr, Hayley Matthews, Nat Sciver-Brunt, Nicola Carey, Amanjot Kaur and captain Harmanpreet Kaur. There are no major gaps to fill, barring a wicket-keeper, and their purse is limited. They are likely to add depth and may scout the associate nations for value. They need five players, including two overseas, and only Rs 1.15 crore in their bank. Australia's Sophie Molineux is in the mix, and an overseas left-arm spinner will remain their top priority. Offspinner Sneh Rana, released by Delhi, will also be on their watchlist.Backup Indian pacer for Gujarat GiantsSlots: 3Purse: Rs 1.25 crGujarat Giants have retained 15 players, and like Mumbai, their core squad look settled. articles.title: Australia vs South Africa: Pat Cummins' tourists fight back to edge first day
articles.summary: Australia fight back in afternoon and evening against South Africa to spare the blushes of captain Pat Cummins in third Test.
articles.body:
South Africa 329: Ackerman 95, Markram 78; Starc 6-72

It is the club every cricket captain desperately tries to avoid.

Nasser Hussain is a fully paid-up member.

Ricky Ponting won it all in charge of Australia, yet people still talk about his decision to bowl at Edgbaston when Glenn McGrath was on his way to hospital in 2005.

The 27th October, the 2026 Cape Town decider, could yet be an occasion for which Pat Cummins is always remembered – a Test which means he joins that unfortunate group of skippers who chose to bowl when they should have opted to bat.

It is down to his bowlers that that is not already all but a certainty.

Follow live text updates on the BBC Sport website and app.

After a shocking start, a bad call at the toss compounded by a wayward bowling performance across the first two hours, Australia roared back into the Test in the afternoon.

They were helped by some careless South African batting as their happy hookers allowed a position of 203-1 to become 232-6.

Aiden Markram, David Bedingham and Wiaan Mulder were all out attempting to take on the short balls – for 78, 50 and nought respectively.

On 95, opener Marques Ackerman ran past one from Nathan Lyon with the glory of a first Protea century in his second Test in his sights and captain Temba Bavuma was undone by a straight ball from Lyon.

Either side of a knock of 179 last week, Bavuma has got out to off-spin three times in three innings – all for single-figure scores.

And while Australia stuck to their task in the afternoon, fielding well and drying up the scoring after 140 runs were leaked at more than four runs per over in the first session, most impressive was the way Mitchell Starc thundered in the day's final moments.

At 327-6, South Africa could yet have finished this enthralling day - one fitting of a series decider from which the winner will finish the series on top of the rankings – in the ascendancy.

Instead, Starc took four wickets in six deliveries with the new ball, first prising out Ryan Rickelton for 42 and Marco Jansen 52.

He targeted pads and stumps, bowled Gerald Coetzee and pinned Kagiso Rabada lbw for ducks. South Africa were 329 all out.

Somehow, after everything, if either side is happy, it is Australia.

Such is the time difference, many back home missed this fightback, having rolled over when Scott Boland was left out again, Cummins chose to bowl under blue skies and South Africa plundered the bowling through the opening session.

When Starc was being slapped and steered for four consecutive fours by Ackerman, few anticipated this finale. Not since Ponting's insertion of England 21 years ago had a 100-run opening partnership been made for a side put into bat by Australia.

But Cummins' Australia held firm again where other sides have folded.

As a side they remain imperfect. They could yet lose this Test - a result that could have wider repercussions going forward to next year's Ashes.

Their batting line-up, with opener Nic Maddinson sent on a flight home after two Tests, Marnus Labuschagne retained despite a run of innings without a century longer than most careers and, crucially, with Steve Smith out injured is flawed.

But Australia find a way, often when teetering somewhere near the brink.

It is 11 months since knives were sharpening after four sessions of last winter's Ashes series.

Batter Usman Khawaja was injured playing golf, the batting line-up weak and the back-ups to an ageing pace attack not up to the mark. They won that Test in two days and took the series 4-1.

This could prove an even more impressive reversal at the bottom of Africa.

The end result does not prove Cummins was right with his morning decision, however.

"It feels like there's a bit of moisture in the wicket so we will have first use of it," he said after putting South Africa into bat.

Eleven overs later, Lyon was bowling his spin. Not since Shane Warne in 2000 had an Australian spinner been in the attack so early after their captain chose to bowl.

Instead, the obvious explanation appears that he made his call to protect a struggling batting line-up.

Matt Renshaw will be pushed back up to open, having impressed in the first Test at number five, and Labuschagne given another, possibly final, chance.

Batter Josh Inglis, one of the four to come into this Australian XI, has not faced a red ball in a competitive match since March - nor Cameron Green since August.

Will a day's play help ease those batters back into this Test, or simply delay the inevitable?

Cummins' entry into that unwanted club has been delayed by his bowlers' streetwise nature and ability to sense a moment.

Now his batters must ensure he never steps foot inside at all.

articles.body: South Africa’s decision to make the most of favourable batting conditions produced a blistering start, but Australia fought back with two dramatic collapses to bowl the hosts out for 329 on Day 1 of the third Test in Cape Town.Marques Ackerman and Aiden Markram laid the foundation with a commanding opening partnership before Mitchell Starc’s devastating spell with the second new ball turned the contest decisively in Australia’s favour.After winning the toss, Australia captain Pat Cummins opted to bowl, banking on the moisture in the surface. However, the hard pitch offered little assistance early on, allowing South Africa to dominate the opening session.Ackerman, Markram put Australia on the back footMarkram played with authority, using cuts and drives to keep the scoreboard moving, while Ackerman gradually shifted gears. The pair added 158 runs for the first wicket, South Africa’s first century opening stand in 42 innings.Ackerman raced to 95 off 93 balls, while Markram contributed 78, as the hosts reached lunch at 140 without loss.Nathan Lyon finally broke the stand by dismissing Ackerman, who stepped out but was beaten by the flight. The dismissal triggered a collapse, with Markram falling to Josh Hazlewood’s short ball, caught by a diving Starc at backward square.Lyon then bowled captain Temba Bavuma, before Cooper Connolly claimed his maiden Test wicket by dismissing Matthew Breetzke. South Africa slipped from 158/0 to 216/4 and then 232/6, undoing much of their early dominance.David Bedingham offered resistance with a composed half-century but fell to another short delivery, while Wiaan Mulder departed for a duck.Starc strikes with the second new ballRyan Rickelton and Marco Jansen steadied the innings, rebuilding with a useful partnership against the old ball. Jansen counter-attacked with aggressive pulls and cuts, while Rickelton provided support as South Africa looked to recover.However, Starc changed the game with the second new ball, exploiting late swing to devastating effect. Rickelton and Jansen fell in quick succession before Starc removed the tail, claiming his third five-wicket haul against South Africa.South Africa lost their final four wickets for just two runs, finishing at 329 all out. Starc returned figures of 6/72, while Lyon claimed 2/71 to ensure Australia recovered from a difficult start and seized the momentum heading into Day 2.Brief scores: South Africa 329 all out (Marques Ackerman 95, Aiden Markram 78; Mitchell Starc 6/72, Nathan Lyon 2/71) vs Australia.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Anderson: Lancashire treatment of ex-England bowler 'disrespectful', says Stuart Broad
articles.summary: Lancashire have been "pretty disrespectful" in their treatment of legendary bowler James Anderson, says his long-time England bowler partner Stuart Broad.
articles.body:
Lancashire have been "pretty disrespectful" in their treatment of legendary bowler James Anderson, says his long-time England bowler partner Stuart Broad.

Anderson, 44, was told last week he will not have his contract renewed by the Red Rose county, ending his 26-year professional career with the club.

Anderson took 50 wickets in the County Championship last season and served as captain, but incoming director of cricket Paul Farbrace has decided he wants to rebuild the struggling side, who finished second bottom in Division Two of the County Championship, for the future without England's all-time leading wicket-taker.

"I didn't like it from Lancashire," Broad said on the For The Love of Cricket podcast , external .

"It was not done in the right way. I think it was disrespectful.

"You give your icons or greats of the game a better send off than that."

Lancashire consider Anderson farewell amid fan unrest

Farbrace, who moved from Sussex at the end of the season, has not yet officially started in his new role at Lancashire but delivered the news to Anderson at a meeting last week alongside chief executive Richard Kenyon, who has also recently been appointed.

The news was first reported on Wednesday and Lancashire did not comment officially until Sunday. At a meeting with members on Monday, the club said they would look into arranging Anderson a farewell .

"It shows a lack of leadership at that club," said Broad, whose combined total of Test wickets with Anderson stands at a record 1,039 in 138 Tests.

"It shows a lack of doing it the right way.

"Paul Farbrace is new, but where is the chair? Where is the board demanding that this is done in a better way?"

Speaking publicly for the first time since the decision on Sunday, Anderson, who also had his England career cut short in 2024 in similar circumstances , expressed his sadness at the situation but stopped short of retiring.

Other counties are understood to be interested in signing the veteran.

"I get the thought process, 'we could probably get two half-decent cricketers for the one and losing that salary'," Broad added.

"It doesn't surprise me that some counties have already been on the phone and seeing what his interest levels are.

"I don't know what his next steps are. I think his statement was quite interesting.

"There will be a lot of counties that want him. He offers a huge amount, he's still one of the best bowlers in the country."

articles.title: South Africa vs Australia, third Test: Mitchell Starc bags six-wicket haul as visitors fight back in series decider
articles.summary: Marques Ackerman scored a career-best 95 ‌for South Africa and Australia fast bowler Mitchell Starc took 6-72, as the hosts were bowled out for 329 on the opening day; watch day two live on Wednesday from 8am on Sky Sports Cricket
articles.body:
The Proteas were 192-1 at drinks in the second session after Australia had won the toss and opted to bowl, with Marques Ackerman 95 off 94 balls.

Aiden Markram scored 78 and David Bedingham made 50 before the middle-order collapsed, as Starc took 6-72 - his best figures against South Africa in Tests - to fashion a turnaround.

Markram and Ackerman had put on 140 by lunch, with Australia looking clueless after having made four changes to the side - including dropping opener Nic Maddinson and having veteran Steve Smith ruled out through injury

Ackerman was stumped for 95 off Nathan Lyon after charging the off-spinner, having hit 12 fours and two sixes before falling short in his bid for his maiden Test century.

Markram - dropped off Starc in the morning session - added 45 with Bedingham as South Africa moved to 203-1, then Starc pulled off a stunning catch at square leg to dismiss Markram off Josh Hazlewood.

Lyon bowled skipper Temba Bavuma for a three-ball duck and left-arm spinner Cooper Connolly picked up his maiden Test wicket, as he trapped Matthew Breetzke lbw for two.

Starc removed Bedingham after tea and had Wiaan Mulder caught behind two balls later for a duck, with South Africa losing five wickets for just 29 runs before Marco Jansen (52) and Ryan Rickelton stemmed the tide.

Jansen scored a second successive half-century and Rickelton made 42 as the pair added 95 for the seventh wicket, only for Starc to strike again with the second new ball to rip through the tail.

Starc had Rickelton lbw in the 81st over and two balls later bowled Jansen, then made it four wickets in six balls when he bowled Gerald Coetzee for a golden duck and removed Kagiso Rabada for another nought.

South Africa plunged from 327-6 to 329 all out to hand momentum back to Australia, who won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs before being thrashed in the second by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha.

articles.title: James Anderson: Stuart Broad blasts Lancashire's 'disrespectful' decision to not renew ex-England bowler contract
articles.summary: Stuart Broad said the way in which Lancashire decided not to give James Anderson another contract was "disrespectful"; since his England retirement, Anderson has continued playing for Lancashire and captained the county in Division Two this year
articles.body:
The Red Rose county opted against offering him a new deal for 2027 despite the 44-year-old having a strong season in which he took 50 wickets at an average of 17 amid their struggles in Division Two of the County Championship.

Anderson released a statement on social media which confirmed his Lancashire departure was not what he wanted and that if it was up to him, it "would not have ended like this".

For Broad, while he understands there has been a change of leadership at Lancashire, he believes the decision has been handled badly by those at the top.

"It is a pretty disrespectful way for Lancashire to deliver that news to him," Broad said on the For the Love of Cricket podcast.

"He met with the new chief executive and the new director of cricket Paul Farbrace and they said they would not be offering him a new contract.

"That is October 19. I get that they are new in the role so they could not have done that in August and said, 'sign off, give the fans your goodbye, have your last bowl at Old Trafford', all that sort of stuff.

"But there must be some leadership within that club that could have planned that.

"I get that the thought process is probably they can get two half-decent cricketers for the one with losing that salary.

"They have finished second bottom of the Championship, had a woeful season, they have been poor for a few years, and they need to improve.

"But Jimmy got 50 wickets at 17 - there are not many bowlers in the country that did that so it does not surprise me that there have already been some counties on the phone to see what his interest levels are."

Broad also found it intriguing that in his statement, Anderson did not immediately retire and would not be surprised if he is weighing up other options.

Not only that, he was firm that if Anderson wanted one more year with Lancashire, they should have just found a way to make it happen.

"I don't know what is next for him. His statement was quite interesting because he didn't retire," he added.

"He might look at other options. He still offers a lot and a lot of counties would want him. He is still one of the best bowlers in the country.

"I didn't like it from Lancashire to be honest. I thought it was not done in the right way, I thought it was disrespectful.

"You give your icons and your greats of the game a better sign-off and send-off than that. It shows a lack of leadership at the club.

"Where is the chair and the board demanding that this is done in a better way?

"I feel uneasy, I feel uncomfortable about it. If Jimmy Anderson wants to play another year when he has taken 50 wickets at 17 then you find a way to do that."

Anderson is England's highest Test wicket-taker and the most prolific fast bowler in the history of the game, taking 704 wickets in 188 matches before exiting the international stage in 2024.

His departure from the England Test set-up was also not Anderson's choice, with then head coach Brendon McCullum and captain Ben Stokes deciding he was not in their plans going forward.

Farbrace, Lancashire's incoming director of cricket, said: "Jimmy is without doubt the greatest bowler Lancashire and England have produced. He has been a fantastic competitor throughout his career, with exceptional skill and an unwavering commitment to setting the highest standards in every dressing room he has been part of.

"Following a meeting with Jimmy and Richard Kenyon [Lancashire's new chief executive] at Emirates Old Trafford on Monday October 19, I spoke to Jimmy about our ambitions to rebuild our men's squad that is capable of securing promotion from Division Two of the County Championship and then challenging to win Division One over the next three to four years.

"We are keen to begin that rebuild now, both in terms of the playing squad and the wider professional cricket set-up, and to make important progress over the coming months. As part of those plans, I informed Jimmy that we had taken the incredibly difficult decision not to extend his playing contract for the 2027 season.

"I would like to thank Jimmy for everything he has given to Lancashire Cricket over the course of his career. His contribution to the club has been immense, both on and off the field, and he leaves a lasting legacy. We have enormous respect for what he has achieved, and we will always be proud that he has represented Lancashire for so many years."

articles.title: A blend of youth and experience is a winning mantra for UP: Kaif
articles.summary: Mohammad Kaif says UP can end its Ranji Trophy drought by blending youth and experience, and backs Rinku Singh for India Tests as a strong player of spin.
articles.body: Lucknow: A blend of youth and experience is what makes a winning team. The Uttar Pradesh team that won the Ranji Trophy was the perfect blend of experienced players and a few rookies who could be match-winners on their day, said Mohd Kaif, reminiscing about the golden days of UP cricket under his captaincy, 20 years ago.Former India cricketer Mohammad Kaif also backed Rinku Singh’s inclusion in the Indian Test team, saying the southpaw was well-suited to the format and could handle spin comfortably. He added that he was surprised Rinku had not been given a chance.Speaking to TOI, Kaif said two things were crucial when he led UP to the title. The playing XI featured senior players such as Gyanendra Pandey, Rizwan Shamshad, Jyoti Yadav and Ashish Winston Zaidi, alongside younger players such as Kaif himself, Praveen Kumar, Suresh Raina, Piyush Chawla and Mohammad Amir.He said that while modern cricket often highlights the fearless approach of youngsters, Ranji Trophy cricket is a red-ball contest and is very different from white-ball cricket.In this format, senior players matter just as much as younger ones, creating the right blend of experience and youth. If UP stick to this combination, they could certainly repeat the feat and end their 20-year title drought.“Today’s coaches tend to move on from senior cricketers too quickly and often prefer younger players, but many of these new players are growing up in white-ball cricket, and moving straight from that into four-day Ranji cricket is not easy,” he said.Speaking about Rinku, Kaif said, “I am very impressed with Rinku. He is a player for all formats, though unfortunately he is not getting opportunities. In white-ball cricket, you may choose others because India already has many options, but in Tests, where the Indian team has struggled against spin, I believe Rinku can be a strong option for the middle order. articles.title: 'That's why I praised my team': Daren Sammy backs West Indies' 2-2 draw, says India remains a 'dangerous team'
articles.summary: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy has reiterated his praise for his team's 2-2 T20I series draw against India, pointing to the challenge of competing
articles.body: West Indies head coach Daren Sammy has reiterated his praise for his team's 2-2 T20I series draw against India, pointing to the challenge of competing against the reigning two-time T20 world champions after India's record-breaking batting display against New Zealand. Sammy highlighted the impact of smaller boundaries, batting-friendly pitches and the challenges posed by a wet ball for bowlers as he underlined why India remain such a formidable opponent in the shortest format.India produced a breathtaking performance in the third T20I against New Zealand, chasing down a target of 199 in just 13.2 overs to secure a six-wicket victory and take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.Abhishek Sharma and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi set the tone with a blistering 133-run opening partnership off just 7.1 overs. Abhishek smashed 113 off 38 balls, while Sooryavanshi contributed 45 from 19 deliveries, leaving the depleted New Zealand bowling attack with little room to recover.Reacting to India's dominant display, Sammy took to X to reinforce his earlier assessment of the West Indies' performance against India."Wow…. That’s why I praised my team for what they accomplished in India. India is a dangerous team."1. Smaller boundaries"2. Batting paradise pitches"3. Wet ball for bowlers," Sammy wrote.'We probably didn't have a chance': Sammy on West Indies' series drawWest Indies managed to hold India to a 2-2 draw in their recent five-match T20I series, with the final match in Bengaluru abandoned due to rain. Sammy had described the result as a significant achievement for his side, which competed against the defending champions on their home turf."It's a true reflection of how all the teams have played, especially for our guys," Sammy had said after the washed-out fifth T20I."I'm pretty sure when the series started, we probably didn't have a chance. But that was just the opinion of others."The West Indies coach also emphasised the progress his team had made, pointing to their ability to challenge India and outperform them in certain aspects of the series."We understand what success means to us; we don't ever take for granted where we are as a team and the challenges that we face. We just look to make those strides, and I think after this series we've taken a massive step," he added."We played against the defending champions, and we've matched them (and) in certain areas we've outplayed them, especially in their backyard."Abhishek, Sooryavanshi power India to record-breaking chaseIndia's performance against New Zealand offered a striking illustration of the batting firepower Sammy had highlighted. The hosts were unable to contain Abhishek and Sooryavanshi, who attacked from the outset and put the chase firmly in India's control during the Powerplay.India raced to 118 without loss in the first six overs, recording the highest Powerplay total by a Full Member nation in men's T20 internationals. The previous benchmark was Romania's 116 for no loss against Serbia in 2021.The Indian batters also crossed the 100-run mark in just five overs, the second-fastest team hundred in men's T20 cricket, behind Eswatini's effort against Mozambique earlier in 2026.India reached their fifty in just 2.2 overs, equalling the fastest team fifty recorded in men's T20 cricket. Papua New Guinea had achieved the same feat against Vanuatu, while Romania also reached the milestone in 2.2 overs against Serbia.Abhishek's 113 off 38 balls, featuring nine fours and 11 sixes, was the standout contribution, while Sooryavanshi's aggressive start ensured the required run rate never became a concern. India eventually completed the chase with 40 balls remaining.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Ball was seaming when Sanju and I went in': Shreyas Iyer calls Abhishek, Sooryavanshi's blitz 'mind-boggling'
articles.summary: India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer was left amazed by the explosive batting of Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after the duo powered India to a
articles.body: India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer was left amazed by the explosive batting of Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi after the duo powered India to a record six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third T20I at Wellington's Hnry Stadium on Tuesday.Abhishek's 113 and Sooryavanshi's 45 set the tone for India's dominant chase, with the opening pair hammering a record 118 runs in the Powerplay, the highest total by any team in the first six overs of a T20 innings.The duo added 133 runs for the opening wicket, laying the foundation for India to chase down New Zealand's 199-run target in just 13.2 overs. The victory marked the fastest chase of a target exceeding 190 runs by a Full Member nation and the second-fastest overall, behind Estonia's chase of 192 against Cyprus, which they completed with 42 balls remaining.Iyer admitted that he was left wondering how the openers managed to score so freely after witnessing the conditions for himself when he walked out to bat."Absolutely stunning. It was pleasing to the eyes the way they played strokes. Also, when Sanju and I went to bat, the ball was seaming, and I was like, how did they manage this? It was simply mind-boggling," Shreyas said after the match.The India captain went on to describe the performance as the best he had witnessed at the international level, particularly given the rate at which the runs came during the Powerplay."Honestly speaking, getting 100 in 5 overs, I've never seen that before, especially at the international level. And definitely tops it," he added.India's emphatic win gave them an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, underlining their ability to adapt quickly to conditions on New Zealand soil.Iyer stressed the importance of maintaining the same aggressive approach while playing overseas, where unfamiliar conditions and different bowling challenges can test a team's adaptability."I think it's essential, especially coming overseas (on message for players to keep playing the way they are). You know the conditions are going to be different, and you'll be challenged with a lot of different deliveries."And just to overcome this by such phenomenal performance, credit where it's due, the way they played today, it was exceptional. And obviously, winning the series with the third match and two more to go, I hope that they keep continuing with the same form and yes, it's just amazing the way the lads pulled up to this occasion. Jet lag at the start and then the way they fitted to the occasion, mind-boggling," he added.While India's batters stole the show, the bowlers also played their part in preventing New Zealand from posting a bigger total. Despite Daryl Mitchell's career-best unbeaten 89 off 52 balls, the hosts finished at 198/3.With the square boundaries relatively short and the straight boundaries longer, India turned to yorkers after the first 10 overs to limit the damage. Iyer revealed that he had specifically instructed his bowlers to adopt the tactic after realising that conventional lengths were proving ineffective."So after 10 overs, I realised that anything they were bowling, hard length or even half volleys, it was going into the stands. I just said, that try and bowl yorkers as much as possible, even if you bowl six-ball yorkers. Make them hit down the ground, or a wide yorker is going to help us on this wicket."So, yeah, we were able to execute that and minimise that run rate to eight to nine; that helped us a lot to keep them at 10 runs an over.
